title: Consolidate fallback lease propagation and route pruning
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The smart routing layer currently uses a mix of per-shard lease state, duplicated propagation logic, and several ad-hoc route pruning heuristics. This has caused race windows where fallbacks are triggered unnecessarily under transient capacity pressure and produces noisy telemetry that obscures real SLO regressions.

Goal: Consolidate lease propagation for fallback decisions into a small, well-tested coordinator, eliminate duplicate lock-heavy paths, and centralize the route-pruning window logic so that regional affinity and fallback decisions use the same pruning criteria. The outcome should reduce unnecessary fallback invocations, lower p95 tail latency during short surges, and simplify observability of routing decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A single fallback-lease coordinator service/component is implemented and used by the smart router hotpath (no duplicated propagation logic remains)
Route-pruning logic (prune window and grace rules) is centralized and configurable via runtime flags; router and region proxies converge on the same policy
Benchmarks show <= 10% reduction in fallback-triggered cold starts and measurable p95 improvement under synthetic surge workload compared to baseline
All existing unit and integration tests pass; new tests cover lease races and pruning edge-cases
Deployment can be rolled out incrementally with a canary toggle and safe rollback path
tasks: Write design doc outlining coordinator interface, expected invariants, and tenant/region-level scoping
Prototype coordinator in isolation and add micro-bench harness (local sim of lease storms)
Refactor smart-router hotpath to call coordinator API and remove legacy propagation code
Centralize route-pruning config into routing-config service and wire into region proxies
Add unit/integration tests for race conditions and pruning edge cases
Run staged performance tests on qa cluster, evaluate telemetry, iterate
Prepare rollout runbook (canary percentages, feature flag keys, rollback steps)
notes: Design trade-offs: fully centralizing leases increases coordination but simplifies correctness; chosen hybrid scope: coordinator per-region to avoid cross-region latency while providing a single code path for propagation semantics.
We decided against a global lease master because CI and multi-region failover introduces unacceptable coupling for the initial iteration.
Telemetry: add explicit 'fallback_decision_reason' tag and 'lease_staleness_ms' histogram for post-deploy analysis.
Risk: small window where old callers still reference deprecated propagation function; plan includes compile-time deprecation throws and a 2-week migration window enforced by linting rules.
